cases.name: a child invoked by the root answers the sendTo of the initial state's entry and its parent completes
cases.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > parent to child > should communicate with the child machine (invoke on machine)

cases.name: a child invoked by the initial state answers the sendTo of that state's entry and its parent completes
cases.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > parent to child > should communicate with the child machine (invoke on state)

cases.name: a child that the entry's sendTo takes to its final state moves its parent on by onDone at start
cases.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > parent to child > should transition correctly if child invocation causes it to directly go to final state

cases.name: a child invoked in a region of a parallel root finishes with its output and the guarded onDone completes the root
cases.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > parent to child > should work with invocations defined in orthogonal state nodes (the onDone guard on output.secret as the whole output)

excluded.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > parent to child > should not reinvoke root-level invocations on root non-reentering transitions
excluded.reason: fromCallback is not ported (out of scope for the actor layer): the root invokes a callback that counts its starts and its disposals, and those counts are the test's point; the entry and action counters alone, without the invoke, would not show that the invocation is not restarted

excluded.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > parent to child > should stop a child actor when reaching a final state
excluded.reason: fromCallback is not ported (out of scope for the actor layer): the test spies on the disposal function the callback returns

excluded.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > parent to child > child should not invoke an actor when it transitions to an invoking state when it gets stopped by its parent
excluded.reason: fromCallback is not ported (out of scope for the actor layer): the idle state's callback sendBacks STARTED on a real setTimeout and the active state's sendBacks STOPPED when it starts. The assertion, invokeCount 1 read in the parent's complete observer, is also the order between two actors, which the record does not hold: XState runs the parent's final macrostep nested in the child's forwardTo, before the child's next deferred effect, and the child then still starts its re-entered idle state's callback (a probe on xstate 5.33.2 counts 2 invocations once the step settles, the second throwing; with child machines standing in for the callbacks the oracle records that second start); xactor queues the forward, so the start follows the parent's stop instead (doc: #differences-interleaving)
